questions.prompt: Which seed quality is most important for uniform crop establishment in a maize field?
options: High germination percentage
Bright seed coat colour only
Largest possible grain size only
Strong smell after storage
questions.correctAnswer: High germination percentage
questions.explanation: Seed with high germination produces a more even plant stand, making crop management and yield prediction easier.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify seed qualities that support successful crop establishment.

questions.prompt: What does soil pH mainly measure in crop production?
options: Soil acidity or alkalinity
Amount of rainfall received
Depth of the topsoil only
Number of weeds in a plot
questions.correctAnswer: Soil acidity or alkalinity
questions.explanation: Soil pH shows how acidic or alkaline a soil is, which affects nutrient availability and crop growth.
questions.learningOutcome: State the meaning of soil pH in relation to crop production.

questions.prompt: Which nutrient is most directly associated with leafy vegetative growth in crops?
options: Nitrogen
Calcium
Copper
Boron
questions.correctAnswer: Nitrogen
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is a major component of chlorophyll and proteins, so it strongly supports leafy growth.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise major plant nutrients and their common roles.

questions.prompt: Which livestock record shows the quantity and cost of feeds given to animals over time?
options: Feed record
Breeding record
Field operation record
Milk cooling record
questions.correctAnswer: Feed record
questions.explanation: A feed record tracks feeds offered, amounts, dates and costs, helping a farmer manage nutrition and expenses.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common livestock records and their uses.

questions.prompt: Which term refers to the young one of a cow?
options: Calf
Kid
Lamb
Foal
questions.correctAnswer: Calf
questions.explanation: A calf is the young one of cattle; kid, lamb and foal refer to goats, sheep and horses respectively.
questions.learningOutcome: Use correct terminology for common farm animals.

questions.prompt: Which structure is used to slow runoff by following the contour on sloping land?
options: Contour bund
Deep vertical pit
Random straight drain
Uncovered gully
questions.correctAnswer: Contour bund
questions.explanation: A contour bund is laid along lines of equal height, reducing runoff speed and soil erosion.
questions.learningOutcome: Name structures used to conserve soil on sloping land.

questions.prompt: Which farm input is a renewable organic source of plant nutrients when well decomposed?
options: Farmyard manure
Diesel fuel
Polythene sheet
Galvanised wire
questions.correctAnswer: Farmyard manure
questions.explanation: Well decomposed farmyard manure adds organic matter and nutrients while improving soil structure.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify organic materials used to improve soil fertility.

questions.prompt: Which stage comes immediately after harvesting before safe storage of most cereal grains?
options: Drying
Ploughing
Pruning
Castration
questions.correctAnswer: Drying
questions.explanation: Cereal grains should be dried to safe moisture levels before storage to reduce mould growth and pest damage.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic post-harvest operations for cereal crops.

questions.prompt: Which enterprise mainly produces eggs for sale?
options: Layer poultry production
Dairy goat production
Beef feedlot production
Fish fingerling nursery only
questions.correctAnswer: Layer poultry production
questions.explanation: Layer poultry enterprises keep hens selected and managed mainly for egg production.
questions.learningOutcome: Differentiate livestock enterprises by their main products.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of mulching around vegetable crops?
options: Conserving soil moisture
Increasing wind erosion
Blocking all soil air
Removing all soil organisms
questions.correctAnswer: Conserving soil moisture
questions.explanation: Mulch covers the soil surface, reducing evaporation and helping suppress some weeds.
questions.learningOutcome: State the purpose of mulching in crop fields.

questions.prompt: Which document records all money received and spent in a farm business?
options: Cash book
Herd health chart only
Planting calendar only
Soil profile diagram
questions.correctAnswer: Cash book
questions.explanation: A cash book records cash inflows and outflows, allowing the farmer to monitor liquidity and expenses.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify financial records used in farm business management.

questions.prompt: Which practice involves growing trees together with crops or livestock on the same farm?
options: Agroforestry
Overstocking
Monocropping only
Bare fallowing
questions.correctAnswer: Agroforestry
questions.explanation: Agroforestry deliberately integrates trees with crops or animals to provide products and ecological benefits.
questions.learningOutcome: Define agroforestry as a climate-smart farming practice.

questions.prompt: Which tool is most suitable for measuring rainfall on a school farm?
options: Rain gauge
Spring balance
Soil auger
Milking machine
questions.correctAnswer: Rain gauge
questions.explanation: A rain gauge collects and measures rainfall depth, usually in millimetres.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify weather instruments used in farm planning.

questions.prompt: Which crop is commonly grown in Kenya as a legume for grain and soil fertility improvement?
options: Beans
Sugarcane
Irish potato
Sorghum
questions.correctAnswer: Beans
questions.explanation: Beans are legumes that can form root nodules with nitrogen-fixing bacteria under suitable conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Recognise common legumes and their role in farming systems.

questions.prompt: What is the main product from a dairy enterprise?
options: Milk
Wool
Honey
Timber
questions.correctAnswer: Milk
questions.explanation: Dairy enterprises keep animals such as cattle or goats mainly for milk production.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify products from common livestock enterprises.

questions.prompt: A farmer plants certified maize seed instead of grain saved from an unknown source. What is the best reason for this choice?
options: Certified seed has known quality and varietal identity
Certified seed never needs soil moisture
Certified seed prevents all pests without management
Certified seed grows well in every climate zone
questions.correctAnswer: Certified seed has known quality and varietal identity
questions.explanation: Certified seed is inspected and tested, so the farmer has better assurance of purity, germination and variety.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the value of certified seed in crop production.

questions.prompt: Why is hardening-off important before transplanting tomato seedlings from a nursery?
options: It prepares seedlings for field conditions
It changes tomatoes into legumes
It removes the need for irrigation forever
It makes seedlings produce fruits in the tray
questions.correctAnswer: It prepares seedlings for field conditions
questions.explanation: Hardening-off gradually exposes seedlings to outdoor stress so they establish better after transplanting.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain nursery practices that improve seedling survival.

questions.prompt: A soil test report shows very low available phosphorus in a bean field. Which response is most appropriate?
options: Apply a recommended phosphorus fertiliser or manure source based on advice
Increase plant spacing only and add no nutrient source
Harvest the beans earlier to create phosphorus
Flood the field continuously for two weeks
questions.correctAnswer: Apply a recommended phosphorus fertiliser or manure source based on advice
questions.explanation: A soil test should guide nutrient correction, and phosphorus deficiency is addressed by adding suitable phosphorus sources at advised rates.
questions.learningOutcome: Use soil test information to select suitable fertility interventions.

questions.prompt: Why is crop rotation with legumes useful in a smallholder maize system?
options: It can improve nitrogen supply and break some pest cycles
It makes maize grow without light
It guarantees a market price for all produce
It removes the need for any field records
questions.correctAnswer: It can improve nitrogen supply and break some pest cycles
questions.explanation: Legumes can add biologically fixed nitrogen and rotation reduces continuous host availability for some pests and diseases.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain benefits of crop rotation in sustainable crop production.

questions.prompt: Which action best reduces post-harvest losses in stored maize grain?
options: Dry grain properly and store it in clean, dry containers
Store grain while warm and moist in torn sacks
Mix grain with soil to make it heavier
Keep grain directly on a wet floor
questions.correctAnswer: Dry grain properly and store it in clean, dry containers
questions.explanation: Low moisture and clean dry storage reduce mould, insects and quality deterioration.
questions.learningOutcome: Select practices that reduce cereal post-harvest losses.

questions.prompt: What is the best reason for using a raised seedbed in a poorly drained vegetable nursery?
options: It improves drainage around young roots
It prevents all insect attack
It eliminates the need for fertile soil
It makes seeds mature without sunlight
questions.correctAnswer: It improves drainage around young roots
questions.explanation: Raised beds allow excess water to move away from roots, reducing waterlogging stress and some seedling diseases.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate seedbed design to seedling health.

questions.prompt: A dairy cow's ration lacks enough roughage. Which problem is most likely?
options: Poor rumen function
Higher photosynthesis rate
Improved egg shell strength
Immediate nitrogen fixation
questions.correctAnswer: Poor rumen function
questions.explanation: Roughage supports normal rumen activity and chewing; too little can disturb digestion and animal performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of roughage in ruminant feeding.

questions.prompt: Why should a poultry house have good ventilation without strong draughts?
options: To remove moisture and gases while keeping birds comfortable
To make feeds unnecessary
To stop birds from drinking water
To make eggs hatch without warmth
questions.correctAnswer: To remove moisture and gases while keeping birds comfortable
questions.explanation: Ventilation removes stale air, moisture and ammonia, but draughts can chill birds and reduce performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain housing conditions that support poultry health.

questions.prompt: Which practice best supports disease prevention in a zero-grazing dairy unit?
options: Regular cleaning, isolation of sick animals and planned vaccination
Sharing needles between all animals to save cost
Allowing manure to accumulate under feed troughs
Mixing new animals directly with the herd without observation
questions.correctAnswer: Regular cleaning, isolation of sick animals and planned vaccination
questions.explanation: Hygiene, quarantine or isolation and vaccination reduce disease introduction and spread in intensive livestock systems.
questions.learningOutcome: Select preventive health practices for livestock units.

questions.prompt: Why is colostrum important to a newborn calf?
options: It provides early antibodies and nutrients
It replaces all future feeds permanently
It prevents the calf from needing clean housing
It is mainly used to sharpen horns
questions.correctAnswer: It provides early antibodies and nutrients
questions.explanation: Colostrum contains antibodies and concentrated nutrients that help protect and energise the calf soon after birth.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of colostrum in calf rearing.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of culling unproductive hens from a layer flock?
options: To reduce feed costs and improve flock efficiency
To increase overcrowding in the house
To keep poor layers for breeding automatically
To stop all egg marketing records
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce feed costs and improve flock efficiency
questions.explanation: Culling removes birds that consume resources without producing enough, improving profitability and management.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain reasons for culling in livestock enterprises.

questions.prompt: Which grazing method helps pasture recover by moving animals between paddocks?
options: Rotational grazing
Continuous overgrazing
Random tethering on wetlands
Burning pasture every week
questions.correctAnswer: Rotational grazing
questions.explanation: Rotational grazing gives paddocks rest periods, allowing forage regrowth and better pasture persistence.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe grazing systems that support sustainable pasture use.

questions.prompt: Why are terraces useful on steep cultivated land in highland Kenya?
options: They reduce slope length and runoff speed
They increase gully depth deliberately
They remove all need for crop cover
They make soil erosion faster for drainage
questions.correctAnswer: They reduce slope length and runoff speed
questions.explanation: Terraces interrupt runoff on slopes, allowing more water infiltration and reducing soil loss.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how terraces conserve soil and water on slopes.

questions.prompt: A farmer wants to harvest rainwater from a roof for nursery irrigation. Which storage option is most suitable?
options: A clean covered tank connected to gutters
An open pesticide container beside the nursery
A leaking sack placed on bare soil
A shallow uncovered depression in a cattle path
questions.correctAnswer: A clean covered tank connected to gutters
questions.explanation: A covered tank keeps harvested roof water cleaner and reduces evaporation and mosquito breeding.
questions.learningOutcome: Select safe water harvesting methods for farm use.

questions.prompt: Which practice helps protect riverbanks on farms near streams?
options: Maintaining grass or tree buffer strips
Cultivating to the water edge every season
Removing all vegetation from the bank
Driving livestock repeatedly through one crossing point
questions.correctAnswer: Maintaining grass or tree buffer strips
questions.explanation: Vegetated buffers stabilise soil, slow runoff and filter sediment before it reaches water bodies.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose practices that reduce erosion near waterways.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes gross margin for a crop enterprise?
options: Income from the enterprise minus its variable costs
Total farm assets minus household size
Cash in hand before any sale is made
Rainfall received minus irrigation water used
questions.correctAnswer: Income from the enterprise minus its variable costs
questions.explanation: Gross margin compares enterprise output value with costs that vary directly with that enterprise.
questions.learningOutcome: Define gross margin for farm enterprise analysis.

questions.prompt: Why should a farmer keep production records for each enterprise separately?
options: To compare performance and make better management decisions
To hide costs from buyers permanently
To replace all physical inspection of crops
To avoid planning for labour needs
questions.correctAnswer: To compare performance and make better management decisions
questions.explanation: Separate records show which enterprises are profitable, efficient or risky, guiding future planning.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how records support farm decision-making.

questions.prompt: A milk producer chills milk soon after milking. What is the main benefit?
options: It slows bacterial growth and preserves quality
It turns milk into powder immediately
It increases the number of milking animals
It removes the need for clean utensils
questions.correctAnswer: It slows bacterial growth and preserves quality
questions.explanation: Cooling fresh milk quickly slows microbial multiplication, helping maintain safety and quality before sale or processing.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain value-preserving practices in livestock product handling.

questions.prompt: Which benefit can farmers get from marketing produce through a cooperative?
options: Stronger bargaining power and shared services
A guarantee that no quality standards apply
Permanent exemption from production costs
Automatic rainfall during dry seasons
questions.correctAnswer: Stronger bargaining power and shared services
questions.explanation: Cooperatives can aggregate produce, negotiate better terms and provide services such as storage or input access.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain benefits of farmer groups and cooperatives in marketing.

questions.prompt: What is the best reason for adding value to tomatoes by making paste or sauce under hygienic conditions?
options: It can extend shelf life and increase market value
It removes the need for any packaging
It makes poor quality fruits safe without sorting
It prevents all price changes in the market
questions.correctAnswer: It can extend shelf life and increase market value
questions.explanation: Processing can reduce perishability and create a higher-value product when quality and hygiene are maintained.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how value addition can improve returns from farm produce.

questions.prompt: Which factor is most important when selecting an enterprise for a semi-arid farm?
options: Water availability and drought risk
Colour of the farmer's record book
Distance to the nearest stadium only
Number of unrelated crops in a neighbour's field
questions.correctAnswer: Water availability and drought risk
questions.explanation: In semi-arid areas, water supply and drought risk strongly influence enterprise survival and profitability.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate enterprise choice to agro-ecological conditions.

questions.prompt: Which practice is a key principle of conservation agriculture?
options: Keeping soil covered with crop residues or cover crops
Leaving soil bare after harvest
Burning residues before every rainfall
Ploughing deeply after every light shower
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping soil covered with crop residues or cover crops
questions.explanation: Soil cover protects against erosion, conserves moisture and supports soil organisms in conservation agriculture.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify principles of conservation agriculture.

questions.prompt: How can planting drought-tolerant crop varieties support climate adaptation?
options: They can produce better under limited rainfall than susceptible varieties
They remove all need for land preparation
They make rainfall measurements unnecessary
They prevent every pest from entering a field
questions.correctAnswer: They can produce better under limited rainfall than susceptible varieties
questions.explanation: Drought-tolerant varieties reduce production risk where rainfall is low or unreliable, though good management is still needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how variety choice can reduce climate risk.

questions.prompt: Which farm practice can reduce methane emissions per litre of milk by improving animal productivity?
options: Balanced feeding and better herd health
Letting animals lose body condition repeatedly
Feeding mouldy feed to save money
Keeping unproductive animals indefinitely
questions.correctAnswer: Balanced feeding and better herd health
questions.explanation: Healthier, better-fed animals produce more efficiently, reducing emissions intensity per unit of milk.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate improved productivity to lower emissions intensity.

questions.prompt: Which safety practice should guide any use of crop protection products on a farm?
options: Follow the label, use protective gear and seek qualified guidance
Mix products by smell until they appear strong
Apply products against the wind without protection
Store products in unlabelled drink bottles
questions.correctAnswer: Follow the label, use protective gear and seek qualified guidance
questions.explanation: Safe crop protection depends on approved instructions, personal protection, correct storage and expert guidance when needed.
questions.learningOutcome: Select safe practices for handling crop protection products.

questions.prompt: A maize crop has pale older leaves, stunted growth and poor vigour. Which deficiency is most consistent with these symptoms?
options: Nitrogen deficiency
Iron toxicity only
Excess copper
Too much calcium
questions.correctAnswer: Nitrogen deficiency
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is mobile in plants, so deficiency commonly appears first as yellowing of older leaves and reduced growth.
questions.learningOutcome: Diagnose common nutrient deficiency symptoms in field crops.

questions.prompt: A vegetable crop is repeatedly attacked by the same soil-borne disease after being planted in the same bed every season. Which change is most suitable?
options: Rotate with a non-host crop and improve field sanitation
Plant the same crop closer together
Keep diseased residues on the bed surface
Stop inspecting the crop until harvest
questions.correctAnswer: Rotate with a non-host crop and improve field sanitation
questions.explanation: Crop rotation with non-hosts and sanitation reduce pathogen carryover and disease pressure over time.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply integrated disease management to repeated field disease problems.

questions.prompt: A farmer expects erratic rainfall and wants to plant sorghum, beans and vegetables. Which plan best reduces total crop failure risk?
options: Stagger planting dates and diversify crops according to water needs
Plant all crops on one dry day without considering soil moisture
Use one late-maturing crop only on the whole farm
Leave all land bare until the final month of the season
questions.correctAnswer: Stagger planting dates and diversify crops according to water needs
questions.explanation: Diversification and staggered timing spread risk when rainfall onset and distribution are uncertain.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply diversification strategies to reduce climate-related production risk.

questions.prompt: A soil has high clay content and drains slowly. Which irrigation method and scheduling approach would best reduce waterlogging in vegetables?
options: Apply small measured amounts only when soil moisture indicates need
Flood the field daily regardless of rainfall
Run water continuously until beds are submerged
Irrigate at midday to force rapid wilting
questions.correctAnswer: Apply small measured amounts only when soil moisture indicates need
questions.explanation: Heavy soils hold water for longer, so measured irrigation guided by soil moisture reduces waterlogging and root stress.
questions.learningOutcome: Match irrigation decisions to soil texture and crop needs.

questions.prompt: A farmer wants to improve sandy soil that dries quickly and has low fertility. Which long-term intervention is most useful?
options: Add compost or well decomposed manure regularly
Remove all organic residues after each harvest
Increase bare soil exposure during hot months
Compact the soil with heavy traffic when wet
questions.correctAnswer: Add compost or well decomposed manure regularly
questions.explanation: Organic matter improves sandy soil water holding capacity, nutrient retention and biological activity.
questions.learningOutcome: Select soil improvement practices for different soil textures.

questions.prompt: A dairy cow weighing about 400 kg should receive dry matter feed at roughly 3 percent of body weight. What is the daily dry matter requirement?
options: 12 kg
3 kg
40 kg
120 kg
questions.correctAnswer: 12 kg
questions.explanation: Three percent of 400 kg is 0.03 x 400 = 12 kg of dry matter per day.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate approximate feed requirements from body weight percentages.

questions.prompt: A ration contains only maize bran for growing pigs. Which problem is most likely if no protein source is added?
options: Slow growth due to poor protein balance
Immediate increase in lean muscle growth
Perfect mineral balance for all ages
Complete prevention of parasites
questions.correctAnswer: Slow growth due to poor protein balance
questions.explanation: Growing pigs need adequate protein and amino acids; energy feeds alone do not support efficient growth.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate feed composition to livestock growth performance.

questions.prompt: A farmer notices many ticks on cattle and declining body condition. Which integrated response is best?
options: Improve tick control, inspect animals regularly and manage pasture exposure
Ignore ticks unless animals stop walking
Use the same dirty spraying equipment for all herds
Move cattle into wetter bushy areas permanently
questions.correctAnswer: Improve tick control, inspect animals regularly and manage pasture exposure
questions.explanation: Integrated tick management combines animal inspection, safe control measures and grazing management to reduce infestation and disease risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply integrated parasite control in livestock production.

questions.prompt: A goat kid is weak after birth and has not suckled. Which immediate management priority is most appropriate?
options: Ensure it receives colostrum and warmth promptly
Begin weaning immediately
Separate it permanently without feeding
Start breeding the doe again the same day
questions.correctAnswer: Ensure it receives colostrum and warmth promptly
questions.explanation: Weak newborns need warmth and early colostrum intake to improve survival and immunity.
questions.learningOutcome: Prioritise care actions for newborn livestock.

questions.prompt: In a dairy breeding record, the calving interval is increasing beyond the farm target. Which factor should be investigated first?
options: Heat detection, nutrition and reproductive health
Colour of milk containers only
Number of trees at the farm gate
Shape of the cash book cover
questions.correctAnswer: Heat detection, nutrition and reproductive health
questions.explanation: Long calving intervals are commonly linked to missed heats, poor body condition or reproductive problems.
questions.learningOutcome: Use breeding records to identify reproductive management issues.

questions.prompt: A poultry unit has high chick mortality, wet litter and strong ammonia smell. Which correction should be prioritised?
options: Improve brooder hygiene, ventilation and litter management
Increase stocking density further
Reduce water availability for chicks
Close all openings permanently
questions.correctAnswer: Improve brooder hygiene, ventilation and litter management
questions.explanation: Wet litter and ammonia indicate poor environment, which stresses chicks and favours disease.
questions.learningOutcome: Diagnose and correct environmental problems in chick brooding.

questions.prompt: A fish pond has low dissolved oxygen early in the morning. Which management action is most appropriate?
options: Reduce overfeeding and improve aeration or water exchange
Add more feed immediately before sunrise
Increase fish stocking without checking water quality
Cover the pond fully with opaque plastic
questions.correctAnswer: Reduce overfeeding and improve aeration or water exchange
questions.explanation: Low oxygen can be worsened by excess organic matter, so feeding control and aeration or water exchange help restore water quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply water quality management in fish production.

questions.prompt: A hillside farm has rills forming after storms despite contour ploughing. Which added measure would most directly slow runoff and trap soil?
options: Grass strips or trash lines along the contour
Cultivating up and down the slope
Removing crop residues from the field
Making a bare channel down the steepest line
questions.correctAnswer: Grass strips or trash lines along the contour
questions.explanation: Vegetative strips and residue lines slow runoff, increase infiltration and trap eroded soil along contours.
questions.learningOutcome: Select combined erosion control practices for sloping land.

questions.prompt: A farmer plans to drain a waterlogged field before planting. Which sign best confirms that drainage improvement is needed?
options: Water remains near the surface long after rainfall
Soil warms quickly and crumbles easily
Earthworms are active in moist topsoil
Plants root deeply without yellowing
questions.correctAnswer: Water remains near the surface long after rainfall
questions.explanation: Persistent water near the surface indicates poor drainage that can limit root oxygen and crop establishment.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify field evidence for drainage problems.

questions.prompt: If a 0.5 hectare plot yields 18 bags of maize, what is the yield per hectare?
options: 36 bags per hectare
9 bags per hectare
18.5 bags per hectare
0.28 bags per hectare
questions.correctAnswer: 36 bags per hectare
questions.explanation: Yield per hectare is total yield divided by area: 18 bags / 0.5 ha = 36 bags per hectare.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate crop yield per unit area from farm records.

questions.prompt: A tomato enterprise earns KSh 90,000 and variable costs are KSh 52,000. What is the gross margin?
questions.explanation: Gross margin equals enterprise income minus variable costs: 90,000 - 52,000 = KSh 38,000.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate gross margin from enterprise income and variable costs.

questions.prompt: A farmer can sell mangoes fresh at KSh 15 each or process them into dried slices with higher labour and packaging costs. What should guide the decision?
options: Compare net returns, market demand and processing capacity
Choose processing because every processed product is profitable
Sell fresh because value addition is always wasteful
Ignore labour and packaging when calculating returns
questions.correctAnswer: Compare net returns, market demand and processing capacity
questions.explanation: Value addition is worthwhile only when expected revenue, demand and costs give better returns within the farmer's capacity.
questions.learningOutcome: Assess financial and market factors in value addition choices.

questions.prompt: A farmer wants a loan to expand a dairy unit. Which record will most help show ability to repay?
options: Cash flow record showing income and expenses over time
A drawing of the cattle shed roof only
A list of neighbours' animal colours
A notebook with no dates or figures
questions.correctAnswer: Cash flow record showing income and expenses over time
questions.explanation: Cash flow records show whether the business generates enough money at the right times to meet repayment obligations.
questions.learningOutcome: Use farm financial records to support credit decisions.

questions.prompt: A farm has limited family labour during school term but high demand for vegetables. Which management choice is most realistic?
options: Schedule labour-intensive operations for available labour or hire planned help
Increase crop area without changing labour plans
Plant crops that all need harvest on the same day
Stop recording labour use because it is variable
questions.correctAnswer: Schedule labour-intensive operations for available labour or hire planned help
questions.explanation: Labour planning matches operations with available workers and avoids losses from delayed planting, weeding or harvesting.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan farm operations according to labour availability.

questions.prompt: Which maintenance action best extends the working life of a knapsack sprayer used on a school farm?
options: Clean it after use and store it safely according to instructions
Leave solution inside the tank until the next season
Use it to store drinking water after spraying
Block the nozzle to increase pressure permanently
questions.correctAnswer: Clean it after use and store it safely according to instructions
questions.explanation: Cleaning and proper storage reduce corrosion, blockage and contamination risks while keeping equipment functional.
questions.learningOutcome: Select safe maintenance practices for farm equipment.

questions.prompt: A farmer wants to mechanise land preparation on a small fragmented farm. Which factor should be considered first?
options: Whether the machine size and cost match the farm layout and expected returns
Whether the machine has the brightest paint
Whether all crops can be harvested on one date
Whether neighbours own unrelated livestock
questions.correctAnswer: Whether the machine size and cost match the farm layout and expected returns
questions.explanation: Mechanisation should fit field size, terrain, access, cost and likely economic benefits.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate practical factors before adopting farm machinery.

questions.prompt: A farm manager compares two enterprises with similar profits, but one has much higher price fluctuation. What management response is sensible?
options: Consider market risk and diversify or contract where possible
Ignore price changes because profit is currently equal
Invest all resources in the riskier enterprise immediately
Stop collecting price information
questions.correctAnswer: Consider market risk and diversify or contract where possible
questions.explanation: Profit alone is not enough; market variability affects cash flow and may require risk reduction strategies.
questions.learningOutcome: Include market risk when comparing farm enterprises.

questions.prompt: A farmer applies compost and keeps crop residues on the field. Which climate-smart benefit is most likely?
options: Improved soil carbon and moisture retention
Instant elimination of all weeds
Permanent immunity against drought
No need to monitor crop growth
questions.correctAnswer: Improved soil carbon and moisture retention
questions.explanation: Organic inputs and residue cover can build soil organic matter, improve structure and conserve moisture.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain soil health benefits of organic matter management.

questions.prompt: A farmer in a dry area wants both fodder and soil protection. Which agroforestry option is most suitable?
options: Plant suitable fodder trees on contours or boundaries
Clear all trees to reduce shade everywhere
Plant trees only in the middle of waterways
Use invasive trees without management
questions.correctAnswer: Plant suitable fodder trees on contours or boundaries
questions.explanation: Well selected fodder trees can provide feed, reduce erosion and improve the farm microclimate when placed carefully.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply agroforestry design to meet feed and conservation goals.

questions.prompt: A farm frequently loses topsoil during intense rain. Which conservation agriculture combination is most appropriate?
options: Minimum soil disturbance, soil cover and crop rotation
Deep ploughing after every storm with bare soil
Burning residues and planting one crop repeatedly
Removing all ground cover before the rainy season
questions.correctAnswer: Minimum soil disturbance, soil cover and crop rotation
questions.explanation: The three principles of conservation agriculture reduce erosion risk and improve soil structure over time.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply conservation agriculture principles to erosion-prone fields.

questions.prompt: Which indicator would best show whether a climate-smart practice is improving farm resilience?
options: More stable yields across variable seasons
More bare soil between crops
Higher losses after every dry spell
Less diversity in farm enterprises
questions.correctAnswer: More stable yields across variable seasons
questions.explanation: Resilience is reflected in the farm's ability to maintain production despite climate variability.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify indicators used to judge climate-smart agriculture outcomes.

questions.prompt: A farmer notices aphids on kales but also many ladybird beetles. Which integrated pest management step comes first?
options: Monitor pest and natural enemy levels before deciding on control
Immediately destroy all beneficial insects
Apply any unlabelled mixture to the crop
Stop scouting because natural enemies are present
questions.correctAnswer: Monitor pest and natural enemy levels before deciding on control
questions.explanation: Integrated pest management uses scouting and thresholds so control decisions protect beneficial organisms where possible.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply scouting information in integrated pest management decisions.

questions.prompt: A cassava farmer selects cuttings from disease-free, vigorous mother plants. Which production risk is reduced most directly?
options: Spread of planting-material-borne diseases
Market price fluctuation after harvest
Cost of transporting produce to town
Soil erosion on steep slopes
questions.correctAnswer: Spread of planting-material-borne diseases
questions.explanation: Vegetatively propagated crops can carry diseases through planting material, so healthy source plants reduce that risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain quality requirements for vegetative planting materials.

questions.prompt: A farmer uses a simple mobile app to record daily milk sales, feed purchases and veterinary costs. What management advantage does this give?
options: Faster analysis of enterprise performance and cash flow
Automatic elimination of all production problems
A guarantee that milk price will rise
Replacement of animal health observation
questions.correctAnswer: Faster analysis of enterprise performance and cash flow
questions.explanation: Digital records can organise data quickly, helping the farmer analyse costs, income and trends.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how digital tools can support farm business decisions.

questions.prompt: A class experiment compares mulched and unmulched plots during a dry spell. Which measurement best indicates the mulch effect on water conservation?
options: Soil moisture content in both plots over time
Colour of the learners' notebooks
Number of stones outside the school gate
Height of the fence around the field
questions.correctAnswer: Soil moisture content in both plots over time
questions.explanation: Comparing soil moisture over time directly shows whether mulch helped retain water.
questions.learningOutcome: Select measurements that test practical agriculture hypotheses.

questions.prompt: Two maize plots receive equal rainfall. Plot A has mulch and contour strips; Plot B is bare and cultivated downhill. Which outcome is most likely after heavy rain?
options: Plot A loses less soil because runoff is slowed and soil is covered
Plot B loses less soil because bare soil absorbs all raindrop impact
Both plots must lose exactly the same amount of soil
Plot A must fail because mulch prevents infiltration
questions.correctAnswer: Plot A loses less soil because runoff is slowed and soil is covered
questions.explanation: Soil cover reduces raindrop impact while contour strips slow runoff, so erosion risk is lower in Plot A.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how combined field practices influence erosion outcomes.

questions.prompt: A farmer must choose between a high-yielding maize variety that matures late and a moderate-yielding variety that matures early in a region with frequent end-season drought. Which choice is better justified?
options: The early-maturing variety because it is more likely to escape terminal drought
The late variety because high potential yield always guarantees harvest
Neither variety should be planted because drought removes all choices
The late variety only if no records are kept
questions.correctAnswer: The early-maturing variety because it is more likely to escape terminal drought
questions.explanation: Where rains end early, a shorter-duration variety can complete grain filling before severe moisture stress.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse variety traits against local rainfall risk.

questions.prompt: A dairy farm's milk yield drops after feed costs are reduced by removing protein supplements. What is the best interpretation?
options: The saving may be false economy if lower yield reduces net income
Feed cost reduction always improves profit
Protein supplements affect only coat colour, not production
Milk yield is unrelated to ration balance
questions.correctAnswer: The saving may be false economy if lower yield reduces net income
questions.explanation: Lower input cost can reduce profit if production falls by more than the cost saving.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the link between feed cost, nutrition and enterprise returns.

questions.prompt: A farmer wants to expand from 50 to 200 broilers but has the same house size and ventilation. Which risk should be addressed before expansion?
options: Overcrowding that increases stress, disease risk and poor growth
Broilers becoming layers because numbers increase
Lower ammonia because more birds share the air
Automatic reduction in feed conversion ratio without management
questions.correctAnswer: Overcrowding that increases stress, disease risk and poor growth
questions.explanation: Stocking density must match housing, ventilation and management capacity to protect welfare and performance.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate capacity constraints before expanding livestock enterprises.

questions.prompt: A soil test recommends liming an acidic field before planting cabbages. Why should lime be applied well before planting and mixed into soil?
options: It needs time and contact with soil to reduce acidity effectively
It kills all pests instantly on contact
It acts as a seed and germinates into cabbages
It works only when left in piles on the surface
questions.correctAnswer: It needs time and contact with soil to reduce acidity effectively
questions.explanation: Lime reacts gradually with acidic soil, so early application and incorporation improve its effectiveness.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse timing and placement of lime for correcting soil acidity.

questions.prompt: A farmer has KSh 40,000 to invest. Enterprise X has expected gross margin KSh 18,000 with high disease risk; Enterprise Y has KSh 15,000 with stable market and lower risk. What is the best decision approach?
options: Compare return, risk, skills and market reliability before choosing
Choose X automatically because its gross margin is higher
Choose Y automatically because risk is the only factor
Split the money randomly without records
questions.correctAnswer: Compare return, risk, skills and market reliability before choosing
questions.explanation: Enterprise choice should consider expected returns together with risk, management ability and market conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse financial and non-financial factors in farm investment decisions.

questions.prompt: A farmer's drip irrigation system gives uneven water distribution, with plants near the tank growing better than those farther away. Which investigation should come first?
options: Check pressure, blockages and emitter flow along the lines
Increase fertiliser at the far end without checking water flow
Remove filters to increase dirt movement
Abandon irrigation scheduling records
questions.correctAnswer: Check pressure, blockages and emitter flow along the lines
questions.explanation: Uneven growth can result from hydraulic differences or blocked emitters, so the system should be tested before other changes.
questions.learningOutcome: Diagnose uneven irrigation performance using practical checks.

questions.prompt: A farm records show maize gross margin is lower than beans for three seasons, but maize residues feed dairy cattle. What should the farmer analyse before reducing maize area?
options: Whole-farm contribution including fodder value and rotation benefits
Only grain sales and ignore livestock feed value
The tallest crop in the field at flowering
The number of bags used in the previous harvest only
questions.correctAnswer: Whole-farm contribution including fodder value and rotation benefits
questions.explanation: A crop may support other enterprises, so whole-farm analysis captures feed, rotation and cash effects together.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse enterprise interactions before changing farm plans.

questions.prompt: A mango farmer receives better prices for graded fruit but pays extra labour for sorting and packaging. Which calculation is most useful?
options: Net return after subtracting grading and packaging costs
Total number of fruits before harvest only
Average rainfall during flowering only
Number of crates owned by neighbours
questions.correctAnswer: Net return after subtracting grading and packaging costs
questions.explanation: Grading is profitable only if the price gain exceeds additional handling and packaging costs.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate costs and benefits of produce grading and packaging.

questions.prompt: A group of farmers wants to supply vegetables to a supermarket with strict quality and delivery schedules. Which capability is most important?
options: Coordinated production planning, grading and reliable records
Planting different varieties randomly without communication
Ignoring rejected produce reports
Delivering only when surplus happens by chance
questions.correctAnswer: Coordinated production planning, grading and reliable records
questions.explanation: Formal markets require consistent quantity, quality and traceability, which depend on planning and records.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse requirements for supplying structured agricultural markets.

questions.prompt: A field has declining yields despite regular fertiliser use. Soil tests show low organic matter and compaction. Which interpretation is strongest?
options: Physical and biological soil health constraints are limiting fertiliser response
More fertiliser alone will always solve the problem
Low organic matter improves nutrient uptake automatically
Compaction only affects livestock, not crops
questions.correctAnswer: Physical and biological soil health constraints are limiting fertiliser response
questions.explanation: Compaction and low organic matter restrict roots, water movement and soil life, reducing crop response to nutrients.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse soil health factors that influence fertiliser efficiency.

questions.prompt: A farmer notices herbicide-like injury on a vegetable crop after using manure from animals fed on treated pasture. What is the most careful conclusion?
options: Investigate possible residue carryover and source manure carefully
Assume all manure is unsafe forever
Ignore the pattern because manure cannot affect crops
Apply more of the same manure to dilute the effect
questions.correctAnswer: Investigate possible residue carryover and source manure carefully
questions.explanation: Some residues can pass through manure, so unusual injury should be investigated and manure sources managed prudently.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse potential risks from farm input sources.

questions.prompt: A beekeeping enterprise near horticultural fields has reduced honey yield after nearby flowering weeds are cleared. Which factor should be considered?
options: Loss of forage diversity for bees
Improved pollen supply from bare soil
Reduced need for hive inspection
Automatic increase in colony strength
questions.correctAnswer: Loss of forage diversity for bees
questions.explanation: Bees need nectar and pollen sources across seasons; removing flowering plants can reduce available forage.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse environmental factors affecting bee enterprise performance.

questions.prompt: A farmer wants to use animal manure in a vegetable field while reducing food safety risk. Which practice is most appropriate?
options: Compost manure properly and apply it with enough time before harvest
Apply fresh manure directly onto leafy vegetables at harvest
Store manure beside clean harvested produce
Wash vegetables in water from an uncovered manure pit
questions.correctAnswer: Compost manure properly and apply it with enough time before harvest
questions.explanation: Proper composting and timing reduce pathogen risks compared with fresh manure close to harvest.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate safe organic fertiliser use in food crop production.

questions.prompt: A community irrigation scheme faces conflicts because upstream farmers take water first. Which management approach best supports fairness and sustainability?
options: Agreed water schedules, measurement and user committee enforcement
Allowing every farmer to open canals whenever they choose
Removing all records so no one can complain
Planting only high-water crops at the tail end
questions.correctAnswer: Agreed water schedules, measurement and user committee enforcement
questions.explanation: Shared water systems need transparent allocation rules, monitoring and local enforcement to reduce conflict.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse governance practices for shared farm water resources.

questions.prompt: A farmer wants to reduce aflatoxin risk in groundnuts. Which combination is most appropriate?
options: Timely harvesting, proper drying, sorting and dry storage
Delayed harvesting, heaping wet pods and storing in damp sacks
Mixing mouldy pods with clean pods to average quality
Storing unshelled nuts directly on a wet floor
questions.correctAnswer: Timely harvesting, proper drying, sorting and dry storage
questions.explanation: Aflatoxin risk increases with crop stress, mould and moisture, so good harvesting and storage practices are essential.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse practices that reduce mycotoxin risk in stored crops.

questions.prompt: A dairy farmer records mastitis cases increasing after changing milking routines. Which investigation is most relevant?
options: Milking hygiene, udder preparation and equipment sanitation
Colour of the cow tags only
Distance from the farm to the nearest market
Number of trees around the cattle crush
questions.correctAnswer: Milking hygiene, udder preparation and equipment sanitation
questions.explanation: Mastitis often relates to hygiene and milking practices, so those routines should be checked first.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse management factors linked to mastitis incidence.

questions.prompt: A farmer plans to introduce a new pasture species. Which trial design gives the most reliable local evidence before full adoption?
options: Compare small replicated plots with the current pasture under similar management
Plant the whole farm immediately without comparison
Ask only one buyer about the pasture name
Judge performance from the seed packet colour
questions.correctAnswer: Compare small replicated plots with the current pasture under similar management
questions.explanation: Local side-by-side trials reduce risk and show whether the new species performs better under the farm's conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Design simple comparisons to evaluate agricultural innovations.

questions.prompt: A farmer has crop residues, livestock manure and household organic waste. Which integrated system best uses these resources sustainably?
options: Composting organic wastes and returning compost to crop fields
Burning all residues then buying more fertiliser only
Dumping manure in a stream to remove smell
Leaving residues in the road for animals to scatter
questions.correctAnswer: Composting organic wastes and returning compost to crop fields
questions.explanation: Composting recycles nutrients and organic matter while reducing waste and pollution risks.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse resource recycling options in mixed farming systems.

questions.prompt: A farmer is deciding whether to insure a greenhouse tomato crop. Which information is most relevant?
options: Premium cost, covered risks, expected income and past loss frequency
Only the colour of the greenhouse cover
Whether neighbours dislike record keeping
The number of empty crates in the store
questions.correctAnswer: Premium cost, covered risks, expected income and past loss frequency
questions.explanation: Insurance decisions should compare cost with the probability and financial impact of covered losses.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse insurance as a tool for managing farm business risk.

questions.prompt: A mixed farm in Machakos has declining soil fertility, unreliable rainfall and limited cash. Which whole-farm plan is most defensible?
options: Combine drought-tolerant crops, manure composting, water harvesting and phased enterprise budgeting
Buy the most expensive inputs immediately without soil or cash records
Shift all land to one high-water vegetable crop
Stop keeping records until rainfall becomes reliable
questions.correctAnswer: Combine drought-tolerant crops, manure composting, water harvesting and phased enterprise budgeting
questions.explanation: An integrated plan addresses climate risk, soil health and cash limits together rather than treating one constraint alone.
questions.learningOutcome: Create integrated farm plans that balance biophysical and financial constraints.

questions.prompt: A cooperative wants to supply export vegetables while protecting worker safety and the environment. Which system design is strongest?
options: Traceable production records, hygiene standards, safe input handling and internal audits
Buying produce from unknown farms without inspection
Using unlabelled containers to reduce paperwork
Ignoring rejected lots to maintain delivery volume
questions.correctAnswer: Traceable production records, hygiene standards, safe input handling and internal audits
questions.explanation: High-value structured markets require traceability, food safety, worker protection and consistent quality management.
questions.learningOutcome: Design quality assurance practices for structured agricultural value chains.

questions.prompt: A school farm wants to compare three soil fertility strategies over two seasons. Which design produces the most useful evidence?
options: Replicated plots with clear treatments, baseline soil tests, yield records and cost tracking
One plot per treatment with different crops and no measurements
Changing treatments midway without recording dates
Using only learners' opinions after harvest
questions.correctAnswer: Replicated plots with clear treatments, baseline soil tests, yield records and cost tracking
questions.explanation: Replication, consistent treatments and measured biological plus economic outcomes make the trial more reliable.
questions.learningOutcome: Create field trial plans that generate reliable agricultural evidence.

questions.prompt: A dairy unit wants to lower emissions intensity without reducing income. Which strategy is most coherent?
options: Improve feed quality, herd health, manure management and reproductive efficiency
Keep more low-yielding animals without changing feed
Reduce milk hygiene to save water
Stop measuring milk yield and feed use
questions.correctAnswer: Improve feed quality, herd health, manure management and reproductive efficiency
questions.explanation: Efficient animals and better manure handling can maintain or raise output while reducing emissions per unit of product.
questions.learningOutcome: Design livestock management strategies that improve productivity and reduce emissions intensity.

questions.prompt: A farmer has one acre near a town, access to irrigation and high labour availability. Which enterprise planning approach is most suitable?
options: Compare intensive high-value crops using market demand, water cost, labour and risk records
Choose the crop with the largest seed packet picture
Plant low-value crops randomly because land is small
Ignore market timing because irrigation is available
questions.correctAnswer: Compare intensive high-value crops using market demand, water cost, labour and risk records
questions.explanation: Small irrigated land near markets can support intensive enterprises, but planning must compare profit, labour, water and market timing.
questions.learningOutcome: Create enterprise choices that fit resource endowment and market opportunity.

questions.prompt: A watershed has upstream cultivation, downstream silted water pans and livestock water shortages. Which intervention package is most appropriate?
options: Contour conservation upstream, protected riparian buffers, desilting plans and water-use rules
Deepening gullies so water moves faster downstream
Removing all vegetation near streams to expose channels
Letting each farmer solve the problem alone without coordination
questions.correctAnswer: Contour conservation upstream, protected riparian buffers, desilting plans and water-use rules
questions.explanation: Watershed problems need coordinated land, water and governance measures across upstream and downstream users.
questions.learningOutcome: Create integrated conservation plans for shared water catchments.

questions.prompt: A horticulture farmer wants to reduce pest losses while avoiding unnecessary pesticide use. Which IPM programme is best designed?
options: Regular scouting, action thresholds, resistant varieties, sanitation, biological control and safe approved interventions when needed
Routine spraying every day regardless of pest levels
Using only one control method and never checking results
Waiting until the crop is destroyed before any monitoring
questions.correctAnswer: Regular scouting, action thresholds, resistant varieties, sanitation, biological control and safe approved interventions when needed
questions.explanation: A strong IPM programme combines prevention, monitoring and targeted control while protecting people and beneficial organisms.
questions.learningOutcome: Design integrated pest management programmes for horticultural crops.

questions.prompt: A farmer wants to adopt solar-powered irrigation. Which feasibility analysis is most complete?
options: Water source reliability, pump capacity, crop water needs, cost recovery, maintenance and environmental impact
Only whether the panels look modern
Only the number of sunny days in one week
Only the highest possible pump price
questions.correctAnswer: Water source reliability, pump capacity, crop water needs, cost recovery, maintenance and environmental impact
questions.explanation: Irrigation investment should match water supply, technology capacity, crop demand, economics and sustainability.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate farm technologies using technical, economic and environmental criteria.

questions.prompt: A county extension team wants to promote climate-smart agriculture among smallholders. Which monitoring framework is most useful?
options: Track productivity, adaptation benefits, emissions-related practices, costs and farmer adoption over time
Count only the number of posters printed
Measure yield once without noting weather or management
Record only attendance at the launch meeting
questions.correctAnswer: Track productivity, adaptation benefits, emissions-related practices, costs and farmer adoption over time
questions.explanation: Climate-smart agriculture has multiple goals, so monitoring should include production, resilience, mitigation, economics and uptake.
questions.learningOutcome: Design indicators for evaluating climate-smart agriculture programmes.

questions.prompt: A farm faces repeated drought, feed shortages and crop residue burning. Which integrated crop-livestock strategy is strongest?
options: Grow dual-purpose crops, conserve fodder, compost manure and plan residue use before the dry season
Burn residues quickly to clear land and buy feed later without budgeting
Keep more animals while reducing fodder production
Stop planting legumes because livestock need only cereal residues
questions.correctAnswer: Grow dual-purpose crops, conserve fodder, compost manure and plan residue use before the dry season
questions.explanation: Integrated crop-livestock planning links feed supply, soil fertility and drought preparedness, reducing waste and production risk.
questions.learningOutcome: Create integrated systems that improve feed security, soil health and climate resilience.
